cards.title: French Air Force Rank
cards.body: French ranks are similar to US. Address as 'Mon capitaine' (Captain) or 'Mon colonel' (Colonel). Use 'Monsieur' (Mr.) or 'Madame' (Ms.) with last name for civilians. Avoid familiarity until invited.
doThis: Ask about preferred address if unsure

cards.title: French Face and Refusal
cards.body: French value politeness. Criticism is best given privately. Disagreement is common but should be respectful. 'Non' means no, but may be softened with 'peut-être' (maybe).
doThis: Be direct but polite when disagreeing

cards.body: French military culture values hierarchy. Address superiors by their rank and last name initially. Use 'vous' for formal 'you'. Wait for them to suggest using first names.

cards.title: Saying No Without Offense
cards.body: French people may say 'non' directly. To soften refusal, use phrases like 'je ne pense pas' or 'ce n'est pas possible'. Explain reasons calmly. Civilians may appreciate polite persistence.

cards.body: French communication is direct but polite. Save face by avoiding public criticism. Disagree respectfully and use 'je ne pense pas que...' or 'peut-être que...'. 'Non' is straightforward; alternatives are rare. Security staff may be strict; have ID ready.

cards.title: Criticism: French Civilians
cards.body: French civilians value politeness and indirectness. Criticize privately, prefacing with positives. Disagree respectfully, using 'Je comprends, mais...' (I understand, but...) to save face.

cards.title: Religion: Respect Catholic Traditions
cards.body: France is a secular country, but Catholicism has historical influence. Respect religious sites and customs, like removing hats in churches. Discuss religion only if locals initiate.
avoidThis: Discuss religion unless initiated by locals.

cards.title: Gift Giving: Hierarchy Matters
cards.body: Gifts show respect for rank. Present gifts to seniors first. Gifts are usually opened later, privately. Avoid expensive gifts; they may be seen as bribes.
doThis: Address seniors by their rank and last name (e.g., 'Colonel Dupont').
avoidThis: Use first names with seniors unless invited.

cards.title: Gift Refusal: Saving Face
cards.body: French may refuse gifts politely to avoid obligation. They might say 'It's too kind' or 'I couldn't'. Insist lightly. If they still refuse, respect their decision.

Respect their decision if they still refuse.

cards.title: French Meal Customs
cards.body: Meals are social events. Wait for the host to say 'Bon appétit' before eating. Keep hands visible and above the table. Bread is part of the meal, not separate. Compliment the food to show appreciation.
doThis: Wait for the host to start eating.
avoidThis: Don't cut salad with a knife.

cards.title: Radio Etiquette in France
cards.body: French radio communication is formal. Identify yourself before speaking. Use 'à vous' to end transmissions. Speak clearly and concisely.
